rationale: The best scaffold (round 5) passes speak_and_act on 99/108 rows (0.9167), and the gate compares against best-so-far (round 4 tied 0.833 and was reverted). A keep needs more than +0.03, so at least 103/108 (+4 rows). Only 9 rows still fail. S06 and S34 (all 3 repeats, 6 rows) are already-disputed labels: the agent gives the instruction-change goodbye, so I do not tune to them. S29 (voicemail) fails 3 rows. In r1 and r3 the agent speaks the correct 'I'll reach out later, goodbye' and calls end_call, but DeepSeek's tool-call markup (<｜DSML｜ calls>) and unrelated rambling leak into the spoken text. That is a model/parsing artifact a prompt rule is unlikely to fix. In r2 it repeats rung 2 instead of closing. Fixing all of S29 gives at most +3 rows (0.944, +0.028), below the 0.03 bar. Latency is also tight: the median rose from 629ms to 675ms over the kept rounds, leaving ~25ms under the 700ms limit, so adding prompt text risks a revert. A temperature or model change could fix S29 but would only add noise to the 99 passing rows with no route to +4. Noop is the safer call. Worth checking outside the prompt loop: DSML leakage in the engine's DeepSeek tool-call parsing.
